categories.definition: Makes a system's outputs, behaviour, uncertainty or current state inspectable, so people can understand what it is doing and judge its results.
categories.label: Explaining system behaviour
categories.question: Which aspect of the system is made inspectable?
categories.rationale: Separate the explanation of one result, the running process, the model across cases, and the limits of what it can establish.

recorded_forms.definition: The system states why it produced this particular output, recommendation, ranking or action. Covers per-case justifications and rationale maps. Not general model description (VA003) and not feature-weight attribution (VA002).

example.title: Beyond the Waiting Room: Patient’s Perspectives on the Conversational Nuances of Pre-Consultation Chatbots

recorded_forms.label: Rationale for a specific machine output
recorded_forms.reason: A local rationale is an applicable form of justifying a particular output.

recorded_forms.definition: Which inputs, attributes or factors drove a result, with weights, ranks, directions or an itemised breakdown. Includes cost or score breakdowns into contributing terms. Not spatial saliency (VA004).

example.title: Visual Analytics for Fine-grained Text Classification Models and Datasets

recorded_forms.label: Feature or factor contribution to an outcome
recorded_forms.reason: Factor contributions instantiate attribution, without making all rationale formats interchangeable.

categories.definition: Connects a result to its sources, supporting evidence or underlying cases, so people can trace where it came from and check its basis.
categories.label: Sources and evidence
categories.question: How can a result be traced or checked?
categories.rationale: Tracing origin and derivation, opening underlying cases, and assessing evidence answer different checking questions.

recorded_forms.definition: A path from an aggregate, flag or summary view down to the individual records, examples or raw data behind it. Overview-to-detail inspection. Not a citation to an external source (VA011).

example.title: Topic Tomographies (TopTom): a visual approach to distill information from media streams

recorded_forms.label: Drill-down from summary to underlying instances
recorded_forms.reason: The recorded drill-down form directly connects a summary with its instances.

categories.definition: Condenses or interprets content through summaries, labels, profiles or a change of representation, so people can grasp what it means.
categories.label: Summarising and labelling content
categories.question: How is content condensed, interpreted or recast?
categories.rationale: Distinguish reducing a body of content, characterising an item, and changing representational kind.

recorded_forms.definition: One document, interview, conversation, video or thread restated shorter so the person gets its gist without reading it whole. Not an overview of a collection (VA015) and not themes across items (VA022).

example.title: GenGO: ACL Paper Explorer with Semantic Features

recorded_forms.label: Condensed summary of a single item
recorded_forms.reason: A single-item summary is a concrete condensation form, distinct from a collection overview.

categories.definition: Expresses meaning through visual form, language, sound, touch or physical action, including translations and adaptations that make it accessible.
categories.label: Visual and sensory representation
categories.question: Through which form can a person perceive meaning?
categories.rationale: Separate the perceptual carrier, translation between carriers, and adaptations that change how the meaning can be grasped.

recorded_forms.definition: Speech output, audio cues, spatialised sound or spoken branching used to deliver content aurally.

example.title: Leveraging Dynamic Audio-Tactile UIs to Assist Visually Impaired Users in Exploring Line Charts through Tactile Graphic Readers

recorded_forms.label: Spoken or audio rendering of content
recorded_forms.reason: Audio rendering is one recorded non-visual carrier, not a claim that every sensory channel is equivalent.

categories.definition: Arranges information into relationships, groups, levels or sequences, so people can understand its structure and move between the whole and its parts.
categories.label: Organising and structuring
categories.question: Which relationships give material its structure?
categories.rationale: Relations, category membership, granularity, position and statistical structure organise different aspects of the same material and may be combined.

recorded_forms.definition: A node-link display of relations, dependencies or connections among entities, including scored or directional edges. Not a branching record of the person's own exploration (VA092).

example.title: Patterns for Representing Knowledge Graphs to Communicate Situational Knowledge of Service Robots

recorded_forms.label: Relational graph or dependency network
recorded_forms.reason: A relational graph directly instantiates the linking operation.

categories.definition: Places alternatives, cases or states in a common frame so people can examine their similarities, differences and trade-offs.
categories.label: Comparing alternatives
categories.question: What is placed in a common comparison frame?
categories.rationale: The comparand distinguishes candidate selection, variation of the same object, and comparison against groups or reference points.

recorded_forms.definition: Two or more candidates, designs, conditions or sets placed together so their differences can be read off. Juxtaposition, small multiples, comparison spaces and operators.

example.title: Value Compass Benchmarks: A Comprehensive, Generative and Self-Evolving Platform for LLMs’ Value Evaluation

recorded_forms.label: Side-by-side comparison of alternatives
recorded_forms.reason: Juxtaposition is a recorded implementation of comparison between candidates.

recorded_forms.definition: The same object shown in two states across an edit, correction, optimisation or model update, so the change itself is visible. Not recovery of an earlier version (VA050).
recorded_forms.label: Before-and-after or version comparison
recorded_forms.reason: Before/after comparison supplies related states, unlike independent candidates.

categories.definition: Helps people find relevant material and control what is in view through search, navigation, filters, rankings and scope choices.
categories.label: Search, filtering and ranking
categories.question: How is relevant material found and brought into view?
categories.rationale: Defining the request, selecting or ordering results, and moving through material are distinct retrieval operations.

recorded_forms.definition: Narrowing what is shown by attribute, text, threshold, spatial extent or named selection, including slicing a corpus into task-relevant subsets. Not selection propagated across views (VA029).

example.title: From 10 Blue Links Pages to Feature-Full Search Engine Results Pages - Analysis of the Temporal Evolution of SERP Features

recorded_forms.label: Filter, query or search over a set
recorded_forms.reason: The retained query/search form is applicable to constructing the retrieval request; its broad value label is not reassigned to every branch.

categories.definition: Keeps information and work history available through notes, annotations, memory aids and replay, so people can revisit and continue their work.
categories.label: Notes, history and memory
categories.question: What is kept available for continuing the work?
categories.rationale: Separate making or capturing a record, arranging material at hand, and returning to an earlier state.

recorded_forms.definition: Attaching labels, tags, notes, comments or spans to items, anchored to the place they refer to. Not machine pre-labels for validation (VA090).

example.title: Solving Separation-of-Concerns Problems in Collaborative Design of Human-AI Systems through Leaky Abstractions

recorded_forms.label: Annotation and comment capture on content
recorded_forms.reason: An annotation remains attached to the material it interprets.

categories.definition: Lets people state what they want through goals, rules, criteria, examples or structured inputs that the system can act on.
categories.label: Goals and constraints
categories.question: How does a person specify what the system should do?
categories.rationale: Distinguish conveying intent, providing a structured or executable specification, and declaring constraints or evaluation criteria.

recorded_forms.definition: The person writes, curates or revises the standards, triggers or criteria the system will then apply, and sees the effect on results. Not a checklist supplied to them (VA055).

example.title: Solving Separation-of-Concerns Problems in Collaborative Design of Human-AI Systems through Leaky Abstractions

recorded_forms.label: Rule, criterion or rubric authoring
recorded_forms.reason: Rule authoring is a recorded way to state required conditions; the wider value vocabulary also covers criteria.

categories.definition: Lets people change a representation, revise an output or redirect a process through edits, settings, parameters and reversible actions.
categories.label: Editing and steering
categories.question: Where can a person intervene in the work?
categories.rationale: Editing an object, configuring behaviour, steering the current process and controlling commitment operate at different points.

recorded_forms.definition: Sliders, toggles, cutoffs and configuration settings by which the person adjusts how the system behaves or what it is sensitive to. Not a statement of goals or requirements (VA040).

example.title: Exploring Mobile Touch Interaction with Large Language Models

recorded_forms.label: Parameter, threshold or weight controls
recorded_forms.reason: Parameter and threshold controls directly instantiate graded control.

categories.definition: Provides candidate outputs, continuations or a space of possibilities that people can explore, constrain and select from.
categories.label: Generating and choosing alternatives
categories.question: How are possibilities offered and shaped?
categories.rationale: Separate presenting a choice space, producing new content, and bounding the generation process. A continuation is not necessarily a set of alternatives.

recorded_forms.definition: Several machine-generated options for the same request presented together so the person can pick or compare. Paraphrase sets, design variants, candidate edits, seed samples.

example.title: TypeDance: Creating Semantic Typographic Logos from Image through Personalized Generation

recorded_forms.label: Gallery of generated alternatives to choose among
recorded_forms.reason: A gallery permits inspection of generated alternatives.

recorded_forms.definition: The system extends a partial input the person has started: prefix-conditioned sentence, token, translation or mark completion, next-position suggestions.

example.title: Effidit: An Assistant for Improving Writing Efficiency

recorded_forms.label: Completion or continuation of what the person began
recorded_forms.reason: In-place continuation extends the person's existing artifact rather than requiring a choice set.

categories.definition: Lets people try hypothetical changes, probe a system's behaviour or practise in a simulated setting and inspect what happens.
categories.label: What-if exploration and rehearsal
categories.question: What can be tried before acting in the real setting?
categories.rationale: Separate learning how a system responds, constructing a hypothetical world, and rehearsing a person's activity.

recorded_forms.definition: A low-stakes simulated setting for trying an interaction, device or behaviour before or instead of the real thing.

example.title: A Piece of Theatre: Investigating How Teachers Design LLM Chatbots to Assist Adolescent Cyberbullying Education

recorded_forms.label: Practice, rehearsal or simulation environment
recorded_forms.reason: A rehearsal environment is an applicable practice form, without implying measured transfer.

categories.definition: Directs attention or suggests an action, resource or procedure, including corrective advice, consequence previews and warnings.
categories.label: Recommendations and guidance
categories.question: What helps a person decide where to look or what to do?
categories.rationale: Attention and warnings, previews, recommendations, and procedural or corrective guidance contribute different information to an action.

recorded_forms.definition: The effect of a candidate choice, specification or edit is shown before it is applied, including live re-render and re-run of downstream results. Not a what-if probe of the model (VA009).

example.title: CapTune: Adapting Non-Speech Captions With Anchored Generative Models

recorded_forms.label: Preview of the consequence before committing
recorded_forms.reason: A consequence preview concerns an action before commitment, unlike a retrospective comparison.

categories.definition: Shows how work is progressing or how a result meets a goal, criterion or reference. It includes feedback on attempts, problem diagnosis, quality assessments and checks.
categories.label: Feedback and checking
categories.question: What basis is provided for judging the work?
categories.rationale: Separate feedback about an attempt or progress, appraisals and status marks, and an active check against a reference.

recorded_forms.definition: Accounts of what went wrong and why: fault localisation, error subsets, cause explanations, failure-pattern canvases, likely false positives and negatives. Not an alert that something is wrong (VA061).

example.title: ConfusionLens: Focus+Context Visualization Interface for Performance Analysis of Multiclass Image Classifiers

recorded_forms.label: Error and failure diagnosis
recorded_forms.reason: A diagnosis identifies an error or failure; it need not include a remedy.

categories.definition: Provides explanations, examples and orientation, and controls when or how much help is available through staged disclosure, learning paths or changing support.
categories.label: Instruction and paced help
categories.question: What help is available, and when is it available?
categories.rationale: Instructional content, the amount or timing of support, and progression across sessions are distinct design choices. Fading is not automatically evidence of learning.

recorded_forms.definition: Support that changes level in response to how the person is doing: escalating from a hint to an answer, routed retry or scaffold sub-dialogs.

example.title: Exploring the Design Space of Cognitive Engagement Techniques with AI-Generated Code for Enhanced Learning

recorded_forms.label: Graduated help that escalates or fades by response
recorded_forms.reason: Response-contingent help instantiates graduated support, with no inferred outcome.

recorded_forms.definition: Illustrative instances, good-versus-bad cases, concretising images or tutorials that show the person how something is done. Not retrieved evidence for a claim (VA013).

example.title: Effidit: An Assistant for Improving Writing Efficiency

recorded_forms.label: Worked or contrastive examples as instruction
recorded_forms.reason: A worked example supplies something concrete to study or imitate.

categories.definition: Organises work into stages, loops, roles and decision points, with ways to coordinate actions, hand work over, recover from problems and resume later.
categories.label: Structuring the workflow
categories.question: How are stages, responsibilities and continuity arranged?
categories.rationale: Separate progression through work, allocation of actions and authority, and continuity across interruptions or handoffs.

recorded_forms.definition: The system asks a narrowing question, confirms its parse, announces a misunderstanding, or redirects an off-track exchange. Not a graduated escalation of help (VA093).

example.title: Chatbots for Data Collection in Surveys: A Comparison of Four Theory-Based Interview Probes

recorded_forms.label: System move that clarifies, confirms or repairs
recorded_forms.reason: A clarification or repair move can restore a broken interaction without implying a new workflow stage.

categories.definition: Asks people to express their goals, questions, explanations or reflections, making their own reasoning available to the work.
categories.label: Questions and reflection prompts
categories.question: Which part of a person's thinking is elicited?
categories.rationale: The object of the prompt distinguishes needs, an account of reasoning, inquiry about the material, and reflection on one's own thinking.

recorded_forms.definition: An invitation to consider one's own state, behaviour or reasoning, rather than to act on the task object.

example.title: MindShift: Leveraging Large Language Models for Mental-States-Based Problematic Smartphone Use Intervention

recorded_forms.label: Reflection or self-assessment prompt
recorded_forms.reason: Self-assessment is a recorded metacognitive prompt, not a measured gain by itself.

categories.definition: Makes people's contributions and viewpoints available to one another through shared representations, structured discussion, role framing and control over what is disclosed.
categories.label: Shared views and perspectives
categories.question: How do contributions and viewpoints become shared?
categories.rationale: Separate shared artifacts and awareness, the framing and exchange of perspectives, and control of disclosure.

recorded_forms.definition: A canvas, collection or space several people act in together, with contributions visible to all.

example.title: Cultivating Spoken Language Technologies for Unwritten Languages

recorded_forms.label: Shared workspace for joint work
recorded_forms.reason: A jointly used workspace is a recorded form of co-construction, without equating shared access with equal participation.

FC001.definition: The system justifies a particular output, decision or prediction so a person can judge why it came out that way. Includes local explanation, decision-path and rationale displays. Not a stepwise trace of the computation and not a global behaviour summary.

examples.title: Generating and Understanding Personalized Explanations in Hybrid Recommender Systems
Personalized Explanations for Hybrid Recommender Systems

FC001.label: output rationale exposed

FC002.definition: Shows which inputs, features, regions or components drove a specific output, as weights, overlays, highlights or ranked evidence. Attribution of causal share to parts. Not general rationale prose, not attention cueing for the person's own task.

examples.title: GNNLens: A Visual Analytics Approach for Prediction Error Diagnosis of Graph Neural Networks
Effects of Explanations in AI-Assisted Decision Making: Principles and Comparisons

FC002.label: feature attribution for an output

FC003.definition: Characterises how a model or algorithm behaves across many cases: population-level patterns, learned rules, class relations, aggregate influence. Not a single output's justification and not a data overview about the world.

examples.title: The Influence of Curiosity Traits and On-Demand Explanations in AI-Assisted Decision-Making
The Author’s Journey—Understanding and Improving the Authoring Process of Theory-Driven Socially Intelligent Agents

FC003.label: global model-behaviour summary

FC004.definition: Makes doubt legible: confidence scores, error bars, ambiguity flags, reliability cues, uncertainty-annotated results. The operation is exposing how much to trust. Not the distribution of data itself.

examples.title: Generation Probabilities Are Not Enough: Uncertainty Highlighting in AI Code Completions
Balancing the Unknown: Exploring Human Reliance on AI Advice under Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty

FC004.label: uncertainty and confidence exposed

FC005.definition: Declares what the system is, can and cannot do, where its knowledge stops, or that content is machine-made: model-boundary disclosure, AI-use status, provenance-of-generation marking, epistemic status. Not per-output confidence.

examples.title: Researching AI Legibility through Design
Towards a Systematic Model of the Effects of Transparency Utterances on Calibrating Trust in Social Robots

FC005.label: capability and knowledge-boundary disclosure

FC006.definition: Shows what the system or a shared process is doing right now: workflow state, conversational state, latency, pending work, agent activity. State of the running process, not of a stored artifact. Not progress against a goal.

examples.title: ExplAIn Yourself! Transparency for Positive UX in Autonomous Driving
Weaving Sound Information to Support Real-Time Sensemaking of Auditory Environments: Co-Designing with a DHH User

FC006.label: live process-state visibility

FC007.definition: Renders otherwise hidden internal structure inspectable: latent spaces, learned concepts, embeddings, hidden variables, layer activations, model-state distributions. Not the reasoning steps, not the rationale for one output.

examples.title: Visual Analytics Using Tensor Unified Linear Comparative Analysis
Predicting Interaction Quality Aspects Using Level-Based Scores for Conversational Agents

FC007.label: internal or latent state surfaced

FC008.definition: Lays out the sequence of steps by which a result was produced so it can be followed or audited: reasoning traces, layerwise process traces, execution provenance, decision-process exposition. Not the conclusion's justification alone.

examples.title: Diffusion Explainer: Visual Explanation for Text-to-image Stable Diffusion
Explanations Can Reduce Overreliance on AI Systems During Decision-Making

FC008.label: stepwise reasoning or execution trace

FC009.definition: Ties a claim, answer or derived item back to the material it came from: citations, source grounding, attribution to a document, speaker or record. The operation is anchoring meaning in its origin. Not drill-down through an aggregate.

examples.title: Bridging Instead of Replacing Online Coding Communities with AI through Community-Enriched Chatbot Designs
From Paper to Card: Transforming Design Implications with Generative AI

FC009.label: output-to-source provenance link

FC010.definition: Moves from a summary, cluster or pattern to the individual cases beneath it, and back. Includes overview-to-evidence tracing and instance-grounding drill-down. Not general navigation, not a static citation.

examples.title: LayerFlow: Layer-wise Exploration of LLM Embeddings using Uncertainty-aware Interlinked Projections
Visual Comparison of Language Model Adaptation

FC010.label: aggregate-to-instance drill-down

FC011.definition: Assembles supporting or contradicting evidence so a person can check a claim or output: evidence tables, claim-evidence confrontation, cross-checking, sufficiency rationale. Emphasis on adjudicating truth, not on tracing origin.

examples.title: JailbreakHunter: A Visual Analytics Approach for Jailbreak Prompts Discovery from Large-Scale Human-LLM Conversational Datasets
The Effects of Interactive AI Design on User Behavior: An Eye-tracking Study of Fact-checking COVID-19 Claims

FC011.label: evidence presented for verification

FC012.definition: Records what the person or pipeline did so the derivation of a work product can be reviewed, reproduced or recovered: analytic provenance, operation capture, versioned lineage, governance records. Not replay for sensemaking.

examples.title: The HaLLMark Effect: Supporting Provenance and Transparent Use of Large Language Models in Writing with Interactive Visualization
Comparing Native and Non-native English Speakers’ Behaviors in Collaborative Writing through Visual Analytics

FC012.label: analytic-history provenance capture

FC013.definition: Arranges meaning in levels of containment: taxonomies, trees, nested goals, part-whole hierarchies, hierarchical navigation. The organising relation is subordination. Not levels of detail on one object, not flat clustering.

examples.title: Abstraction Alignment: Comparing Model-Learned and Human-Encoded Conceptual Relationships
Towards More Accessible Scientific PDFs for People with Visual Impairments: Step-by-Step PDF Remediation to Improve Tag Accuracy

FC013.label: hierarchical or nested organisation

FC014.definition: Compresses a body of material into a single inspectable whole: corpus overviews, dataset landscapes, at-a-glance summaries, aggregate visualisations. Gives orientation over many items. Not condensation of one text, not a statistical distribution.

examples.title: Visual Analytics for Fine-grained Text Classification Models and Datasets
What makes web data tables accessible? Insights and a tool for rendering accessible tables for people with visual impairments

FC014.label: overview or aggregate gist

FC015.definition: Represents entities and the links among them: dependency maps, causal graphs, stakeholder relations, co-occurrence networks, concept maps. The operation is exposing relations. Not similarity grouping, not containment.

examples.title: TeamVision: An AI-powered Learning Analytics System for Supporting Reflection in Team-based Healthcare Simulation
Deconstructing Depression Stigma: Integrating AI-driven Data Collection and Analysis with Causal Knowledge Graphs

FC015.label: relational or network map

FC016.definition: Gathers items by likeness into groups, neighbourhoods or a similarity space: clusters, similarity overviews, semantic grouping of work items, redundancy-aware source grouping. Not user-defined category schemes.

examples.title: Prismatic: Interactive Multi-View Cluster Analysis of Concept Stocks
How Do Visual Explanations Foster End Users’ Appropriate Trust in Machine Learning?

FC016.label: similarity grouping and clustering

FC017.definition: Supplies a bounded set of meaning categories, codes, tags or terms to think and speak with: coding frameworks, annotation vocabularies, shared terminology, activity-state vocabularies. Supplying the scheme, not applying it.

examples.title: From Granular Grief to Binary Belief: A Collaborative Optimization of Annotation Techniques for Anti-Autistic Language
#lets-discuss: Analyzing Student Affect in Course Forums Using Emoji

FC017.label: categorisation scheme or controlled vocabulary

FC018.definition: Breaks a task, artifact, claim or process into constituent units so each can be handled: procedural decomposition, functional decomposition, decomposed claims, sub-goal structuring. Not hierarchy as a browsing structure.

examples.title: Rambler: Supporting Writing With Speech via LLM-Assisted Gist Manipulation
Iterative Research Idea Development Through Evolving and Composing Idea Facets with Literature-Grounded Feedback

FC018.label: decomposition into parts

FC019.definition: Lets a person move between an overview and more detailed views while keeping the surrounding context.

examples.title: Topic Tomographies (TopTom): a visual approach to distill information from media streams
WhatELSE: Shaping Narrative Spaces at Configurable Level of Abstraction for AI-bridged Interactive Storytelling

FC019.label: multiscale detail and semantic zoom

FC020.definition: Organises material along time: timelines, event sequencing, temporal maps, playback position, calendar structure, temporal pattern views. Arranging in time, not comparing across time and not history replay.

examples.title: CoKnowledge: Supporting Assimilation of Time-synced Collective Knowledge in Online Science Videos
From Protests on the Streets to a War in the East: Evolution of Discourse in a Prolonged Crisis

FC020.label: temporal arrangement of material

FC021.definition: Organises meaning by position in a space: layout specification, spatial grouping, maps of place, spatial overviews, context-preserving arrangement. Not a similarity projection whose point is grouping.

examples.title: NeuroMaps – A Compact Fingerprint for Analyzing Brain Activity
RealityEffects: Augmenting 3D Volumetric Videos with Object-Centric Annotation and Dynamic Visual Effects

FC021.label: spatial arrangement of material

FC022.definition: Holds two or more representations, views or modal spaces in registered alignment so the same thing can be found in each: linked views, coordinated multiview, cross-view identity cues, correspondence specification. Not sensory re-encoding.

examples.title: Kori: Interactive Synthesis of Text and Charts in Data Documents
Compositional Structures as Substrates for Human-AI Co-creation Environment: A Design Approach and A Case Study

FC022.label: cross-representation correspondence

FC023.definition: Shows quantitative structure over a population: distributions, frequencies, prevalence, correlations, ranges, central estimates, statistical ensembles. Not uncertainty about one output, not subgroup contrast.

examples.title: TeamVision: An AI-powered Learning Analytics System for Supporting Reflection in Team-based Healthcare Simulation
ClimateSOM: A Visual Analysis Workflow for Climate Ensemble Datasets

FC023.label: distributional or statistical structure display

FC024.definition: Places two or more candidates, outputs, models or designs together for judgment: comparison views, juxtaposition, alternative-output inspection, comparison-frame alignment. Not counterfactual variation, not peer benchmarking.

examples.title: Surfacing Variations to Calibrate Perceived Reliability of MLLM-generated Image Descriptions
What Lies Beneath? Exploring the Impact of Underlying AI Model Updates in AI-Infused Systems

FC024.label: side-by-side alternative comparison

FC025.definition: Shows what would differ under a change: counterfactuals, before/after, contrastive explanation, sensitivity to an edit, consequence of a revision already made. The comparand is a variant of the same thing.

examples.title: BiaSeer: A Visual Analytics System for Identifying and Understanding Media Bias
Cluster-Based Approach for Visual Anomaly Detection in Multivariate Welding Process Data Supported by User Guidance

FC025.label: contrastive or counterfactual comparison

FC026.definition: Positions a person, item or result against a norm, reference standard, expert model or peer group: peer comparison, relative quality benchmarks, comparison to a gold reference, social-proof framing.

examples.title: Sibyl: Understanding and Addressing the Usability Challenges of Machine Learning In High-Stakes Decision Making
Promoting Energy-Efficient Behavior by Depicting Social Norms in a Recommender Interface

FC026.label: benchmark or peer-referenced comparison

FC027.definition: Contrasts defined groups or cohorts against each other: subgroup comparison, fairness disparity views, cohort analogues, group-level perspective distributions, intersectional slices. Not a single distribution.

examples.title: Visual Analysis of Discrimination in Machine Learning
ConfusionLens: Focus+Context Visualization Interface for Performance Analysis of Multiclass Image Classifiers

FC027.label: subgroup or population comparison

FC028.definition: Compares states across time to reveal trend, growth or drift: trajectories, temporal trend comparison, progress over time, model-quality over versions, longitudinal change. Not arrangement in time.

examples.title: MedDecXtract: A Clinician-Support System for Extracting, Visualizing, and Annotating Medical Decisions in Clinical Narratives
ClimateSOM: A Visual Analysis Workflow for Climate Ensemble Datasets

FC028.label: change-over-time comparison

FC029.definition: Narrows a body of material to what matters here: semantic filtering, personalised information filtering, relevance rules, noise suppression, corpus filtering. The operation is exclusion by relevance, not ordering.

examples.title: Scholar Inbox: Personalized Paper Recommendations for Scientists
Exploring Multidimensional Checkworthiness: Designing AI-assisted Claim Prioritization for Human Fact-checkers

FC029.label: relevance filtering of a corpus

FC030.definition: Lets a person build, edit or inspect the query that retrieves material: editable query representations, faceted query building, query expansion, visual query steering, attribute-guided search.

examples.title: HiRegEx: Interactive Visual Query and Exploration of Multivariate Hierarchical Data
From 10 Blue Links Pages to Feature-Full Search Engine Results Pages - Analysis of the Temporal Evolution of SERP Features

FC030.label: query construction and search specification

FC031.definition: Pulls in an explanation, definition, record or external source at the moment of need, without leaving the task: contextual lookup, external-evidence access, detail on request, cross-modal reference access.

examples.title: Understanding is a Two-Way Street: User-Initiated Repair on Agent Responses and Hearing in Conversational Interfaces
SplatOverflow: Asynchronous Hardware Troubleshooting

FC031.label: on-demand lookup of related information

FC032.definition: Orders items so the important ones come first: triage rankings, risk salience ordering, prioritised candidates, novelty-directed ordering, ranked lists. Ordering, not filtering out and not pointing at one item.

examples.title: Scholar Inbox: Personalized Paper Recommendations for Scientists
Working with Color: How Color Quantization Can Aid Researchers of Problematic Information

FC032.label: ranked or prioritised surfacing

FC033.definition: Bounds what an analysis, audit or view covers: scope configuration, subset selection, extent constraints, evidence-scope control, scope relaxation. Setting the frame of attention rather than ranking inside it.

examples.title: Emblaze: Illuminating Machine Learning Representations through Interactive Comparison of Embedding Spaces
Sakura: Large-scale Incorrect Example Retrieval System for Learners of Japanese as a Second Language

FC033.label: analytic scope setting

FC034.definition: Moves a person through an information structure and keeps them oriented: navigable overviews, guided traversal, jump-to-position, coordinated navigation, exploratory paths. Not drill-down to evidence.

examples.title: GenGO: ACL Paper Explorer with Semantic Features
SpeechCompass: Enhancing Mobile Captioning with Diarization and Directional Guidance via Multi-Microphone Localization

FC034.label: navigation and wayfinding through structure

FC035.definition: Presents a bounded, enumerated set of meaningful options for selection: option lists, suggestion menus, candidate sets, semantically organised choices, context-conditioned option sets.

examples.title: From 10 Blue Links Pages to Feature-Full Search Engine Results Pages - Analysis of the Temporal Evolution of SERP Features
Ink Restorer: Virtual Restoration of Ancient Chinese Paintings Inheriting Traditional Restoration Processes

FC035.label: candidate or option set to choose from

FC036.definition: Produces multiple variant outputs so the person can explore possibility rather than accept one answer: generated variations, alternative drafts, sampled possibilities, refinement option sets, ideation output.

examples.title: WhatIF: Branched Narrative Fiction Visualization for Authoring Emergent Narratives using Large Language Models
StoryEnsemble: Enabling Dynamic Exploration & Iteration in the Design Process with AI and Forward-Backward Propagation

FC036.label: generated alternatives to explore

FC037.definition: The person sets bounds that the generator must respect: generative constraints, constrained ideation, constraint-aware option generation, sketch- or rule-limited synthesis. Constraint on producing, not on specifying a task.

examples.title: ShoeGenAI: A Creativity Support Tool Bridging Design Intention and Feasibility in Shoe Design
MemoVis: A GenAI-Powered Tool for Creating Companion Reference Images for 3D Design Feedback

FC037.label: user-constrained generation

FC038.definition: Represents the space of possibilities as a navigable terrain: design spaces, parameter-space maps, solution-space navigation, trade-off surfaces, quality landscapes, candidate-space overviews.

examples.title: Investigating How Practitioners Use Human-AI Guidelines: A Case Study on the People + AI Guidebook
Revealing the Unwritten: Visual Investigation of Beam Search Trees to Address Language Model Prompting Challenges

FC038.label: option-space landscape or design space

FC039.definition: Meaning made deliberately less available: faded or withdrawn help, choice-limiting structures, display reduction, added friction, bounded responses, suppressed detail. Negative content kept as its own operation.

examples.title: Configuring and Monitoring Students’ Interactions with Generative AI Tools: Supporting Teacher Autonomy
Does the Whole Exceed its Parts? The Effect of AI Explanations on Complementary Team Performance

FC039.label: deliberate restriction or withdrawal of support

FC040.definition: Proposes what to do next in the work: next-step suggestions, strategy recommendations, coordination directives, action prompts, continuation of a plan. Forward-looking advice not tied to a detected defect.

examples.title: Care-Based Eco-Feedback Augmented with Generative AI: Fostering Pro-Environmental Behavior through Emotional Attachment
Studying Self-Care with Generative AI Tools: Lessons for Design

FC040.label: next-step recommendation

FC041.definition: Tells the person how to fix an identified problem: repair hints, revision guidance, remediation actions, corrective suggestions, improvement guidance tied to a metric or violation. Diagnosis alone is a separate code.

examples.title: User-Driven Value Alignment: Understanding Users’ Perceptions and Strategies for Addressing Biased and Discriminatory Statements in AI Companions
RoboCritics: Enabling Reliable End-to-End LLM Robot Programming through Expert-Informed Critics

FC041.label: corrective or remediation guidance

FC042.definition: Suggests specific content, resources, precedents, people or items to take up, often with a justification: recommended examples, precedent suggestions, resource curation for action, recommendation explanations.

examples.title: Infographics Wizard: Flexible Infographics Authoring and Design Exploration
HEPHA: A Mixed-Initiative Image Labeling Tool for Specialized Domains

FC042.label: item or content recommendation

FC043.definition: Points the person at where to look: highlighting, salience cues, anomaly flags, attention overlays, localisation of the thing that matters. Directs gaze, does not prescribe an action.

examples.title: GlideRX: Enhancing Situation Awareness for Collision Prevention in Glider Flight through Extended Reality
Cognitive Forcing for Better Decision-Making: Reducing Overreliance on AI Systems Through Partial Explanations

FC043.label: attention direction and salience cueing

FC044.definition: Signals hazard, harm, violation or impending breakdown so the person can hold back: risk annotations, hazard alerts, validity warnings, breakdown warnings, safety flags. Warning, not diagnosis of quality.

examples.title: Farsight: Fostering Responsible AI Awareness During AI Application Prototyping
HILL: A Hallucination Identifier for Large Language Models

FC044.label: risk alert or warning

FC045.definition: Provides the steps for performing a procedure: task-sequence guides, stepwise procedures, in-situ action guidance, demonstrated procedures, embedded task instructions. Instruction for doing, not a worked exemplar to imitate.

examples.title: SmartRecorder: An IMU-based Video Tutorial Creation by Demonstration System for Smartphone Interaction Tasks
Understanding Learner-LLM Chatbot Interactions and the Impact of Prompting Guidelines

FC045.label: procedural how-to instruction

FC046.definition: Shows what would follow from a contemplated action before it is taken: outcome previews, simulated results of a choice, candidate-remedy previews, authored-consequence previews. Prospective, not retrospective contrast.

examples.title: Teaching the Teacher: Live Foundation Model and Augmented Reality Feedback for Human-to-Robot Skill Transfer
DITTO: A Visual Digital Twin for Interventions and Temporal Treatment Outcomes in Head and Neck Cancer

FC046.label: prospective consequence preview

FC047.definition: The person acts on the represented meaning itself by handling it: dragging, sketching, moving, reshaping, in-place editing of the representation, tangible or spatial manipulation. Acting on meaning, not organising it.

examples.title: ImaginationVellum: Generative-AI Ideation Canvas with Spatial Prompts, Generative Strokes, and Ideation History
AI-Instruments: Embodying Prompts as Instruments to Abstract & Reflect Graphical Interface Commands as General-Purpose Tools

FC047.label: direct manipulation of a semantic object

FC048.definition: What the system produced is offered as a draft the person may accept, correct or override: editable generated drafts, correctable decisions, reversible AI judgments, human-in-the-loop correction of machine results.

examples.title: ArtMentor: AI-Assisted Evaluation of Artworks to Explore Multimodal Large Language Models Capabilities
DocSpiral: A Platform for Integrated Assistive Document Annotation through Human-in-the-Spiral

FC048.label: editable machine output

FC049.definition: Graded control over an amount: sliders, dials, weights, continuous steering magnitudes, adjustable thresholds and levels. The control surface is a quantity, not a discrete option or a settings panel.

examples.title: Exploring Mobile Touch Interaction with Large Language Models
Prefer2SD: A Human-in-the-Loop Approach to Balancing Similarity and Diversity in In-Game Friend Recommendations

FC049.label: continuous parameter or dial control

FC050.definition: Sets how the system will operate: configurable criteria, settings, representation-format choices, view composition, feature toggles, semantics of a display. Persistent configuration, not moment-to-moment steering.

examples.title: CapTune: Adapting Non-Speech Captions With Anchored Generative Models
Generative and Malleable User Interfaces with Generative and Evolving Task-Driven Data Model

FC050.label: configuration of system behaviour

FC051.definition: The person redirects a generation, conversation or analysis while it runs: mid-course steering, relevance feedback, preference nudges during production, redirecting a dialogue, scoped workflow steering.

examples.title: An Analytical Framework for Formulating Metrics for Evaluating Multi-dimensional Time-series Data
Exploring Empty Spaces: Human-in-the-Loop Data Augmentation

FC051.label: steering an ongoing process

FC052.definition: Actions can be undone, branched or tried without commitment: reversible checkpoints, non-destructive experimentation, versioned recovery, low-commitment trials, alternative-history branches.

examples.title: Nabokov’s Cards: An AI Assisted Prewriting System to Support Bottom-Up Creative Writing
Data Has Entered the Chat: How Data Workers Conduct Exploratory Visual Analytic Conversations with GenAI Agents

FC052.label: reversibility and safe experimentation

FC053.definition: The person states goals, preferences or tasks in ordinary language or dialogue and the system takes it as the spec: natural-language goals, conversational preference setting, dialogic goal construction.

examples.title: Context-Mediated Domain Adaptation in Multi-Agent Sensemaking Systems
Bidirectional Human-Robot Communication for Physical Human-Robot Interaction

FC053.label: natural-language or conversational specification

FC054.definition: Intent is conveyed by showing instances rather than stating rules: example-based specification, programming by demonstration, exemplar-defined categories, reference images or cases as the spec.

examples.title: End User Authoring of Personalized Content Classifiers: Comparing Example Labeling, Rule Writing, and LLM Prompting
A Piece of Theatre: Investigating How Teachers Design LLM Chatbots to Assist Adolescent Cyberbullying Education

FC054.label: example or demonstration specification

FC055.definition: The person states conditions the result must satisfy: explicit constraints, behavioural rules, conditional states, relevance rules, regional or structural restrictions authored by the user.

examples.title: FusAIn: Composing Generative AI Visual Prompts Using Pen-based Interaction
Co-Writing Screenplays and Theatre Scripts with Language Models: Evaluation by Industry Professionals

FC055.label: explicit constraint or rule specification

FC056.definition: The person defines or weights the criteria by which things will be judged or ranked: rubrics, decision criteria, criterion weighting, evaluation metrics, quality standards made explicit and editable.

examples.title: Value Compass Benchmarks: A Comprehensive, Generative and Self-Evolving Platform for LLMs’ Value Evaluation
AutoQual: An LLM Agent for Automated Discovery of Interpretable Features for Review Quality Assessment

FC056.label: criteria and rubric specification

FC057.definition: Input is shaped by a provided structure: templates, fields, schemas, question sets, framing prompts that constrain what the person supplies. The structure carries the meaning of what is asked for.

examples.title: Aspirations and Practice of ML Model Documentation: Moving the Needle with Nudging and Traceability
POTATO: The Portable Text Annotation Tool

FC057.label: structured input form or schema

FC058.definition: The person writes something the machine will run or enforce: notation, code, executable specifications, declarative layout languages, visual programs, formal operationalisations of a property.

examples.title: JESSIE: Synthesizing Social Robot Behaviors for Personalized Neurorehabilitation and Beyond
Athena: Intermediate Representations for Iterative Scaffolded App Generation with an LLM

FC058.label: authoring a formal or executable representation

FC059.definition: The system draws out what the person wants or needs before acting: intent elicitation, information-need probing, preference elicitation, explanation-need questions, requirement gathering prompts.

examples.title: Where Can My Career Take Me? Harnessing Dialogue for Interactive Career Goal Recommendations
What About My Design Context?: Exploring the Use of Generative AI to Support Customization of Translational Research Artifacts

FC059.label: intent and need elicitation

FC060.definition: Prompts the person to examine their own reasoning, assumptions, bias or experience: reflection prompts, self-assessment triggers, bias-challenging interventions, retrospective self-monitoring.

examples.title: Remini: Leveraging Chatbot-Mediated Mutual Reminiscence for Promoting Positive Affect and Feeling of Connectedness among Loved Ones
Friction: Deciphering Writing Feedback into Writing Revisions through LLM-Assisted Reflection

FC060.label: reflective and metacognitive prompting

FC061.definition: Shapes how the person interrogates the material: question guides, hypothesis prompts, critical checking prompts, inquiry strategy cues, coverage prompts that push toward unexamined ground.

examples.title: Analogical reasoning with large language models: a co-creative framework and benchmarking of LLMs in design ideation
Collaborative Game-based Learning Analytics: Predicting Learning Outcomes from Game-based Collaborative Problem Solving Behaviors

FC061.label: inquiry and hypothesis prompting

FC062.definition: Draws out the person's account, strategy or explanation in their own words: narrative elicitation, verbalised reasoning, rationale capture before a decision, continuation elicitation, articulation prompts.

examples.title: Chatbots for Data Collection in Surveys: A Comparison of Four Theory-Based Interview Probes
ChaCha: Leveraging Large Language Models to Prompt Children to Share Their Emotions about Personal Events

FC062.label: narrative and reasoning elicitation

FC063.definition: Shows where a problem occurs and what kind of problem it is, such as an error, misconception or quality issue. This diagnosis gives the person a basis for deciding what to revise.

examples.title: A Unified Interactive Model Evaluation for Classification, Object Detection, and Instance Segmentation in Computer Vision
VISPUR: Visual Aids for Identifying and Interpreting Spurious Associations in Data-Driven Decisions

FC063.label: Identifying problems in the work

FC064.definition: Returns an appraisal on criteria: quality scores, critiques, multi-criteria evaluations, holistic match judgments, evaluative advice. The output is a verdict about worth.

examples.title: How Good is ChatGPT in Giving Advice on Your Visualization Design?
Automated Educational Question Generation at Different Bloom’s Skill Levels using Large Language Models: Strategies and Evaluation

FC064.label: evaluative judgment or quality rating

FC065.definition: Reports the result of what the person did so they can adjust: performance feedback, outcome-error interpretation, enactment feedback, action-evaluation cues, response to an attempt. Feedback on doing, not a verdict on quality.

examples.title: Rethinking Teaching Evaluation Reports: Designing AI-transformed Student Feedback for Instructor Engagement
MindShift: Leveraging Large Language Models for Mental-States-Based Problematic Smartphone Use Intervention

FC065.label: formative outcome feedback

FC066.definition: Shows how far along the person or work is against a goal or plan: progress maps, completion indicators, coverage feedback, readiness displays, longitudinal progress. Progress toward a target, not live system state.

examples.title: Relatedly: Scaffolding Literature Reviews with Existing Related Work Sections
Supporting Serendipitous Discovery and Balanced Analysis of Online Product Reviews with Interaction-Driven Metrics and Bias-Mitigating Suggestions

FC066.label: progress and status tracking

FC067.definition: Attaches a discrete status to items: correct/incorrect marks, violation labels, flags, decision-status cues, binary diagnostic indicators, editable-status framing. A compact per-item state token.

examples.title: Leveraging Learner Errors in Digital Argumentation Learning: How ALure Helps Students Learn from their Mistakes and Write Better Arguments
Skeptik: A Hybrid Framework for Combating Potential Misinformation in Journalism

FC067.label: correctness or status marking

FC068.definition: Structures the act of checking an output or claim against ground truth, a rule or a sample: verification workflows, output checks, presence checking, validation against domain rules, confirmation prompts.

examples.title: “Trying to Piece It Together”: Exploring Accessible Error Detection in Emerging Privacy Techniques With Blind People
Automated Extraction and Analysis of Developer's Rationale in Open Source Software

FC068.label: verification and checking against a reference

FC069.definition: Work is organised into ordered stages that unfold in sequence: staged workflows, phase structure, pipelines, sequenced task progression, structured multi-step processes. The operation is imposing order on the work.

examples.title: Visualizing Graph Neural Networks with CorGIE: Corresponding a Graph to Its Embedding
Shiksha Copilot: Teacher-AI Collaboration for Curating and Customizing Lesson Plans in Low-Resource Schools

FC069.label: staged or phased workflow

FC070.definition: Work cycles through produce-inspect-revise repeatedly: iterative refinement, feedback loops, trial-and-revision cycles, repeated curation passes. The operation is recurrence rather than linear sequence.

examples.title: MisVisFix: An Interactive Dashboard for Detecting, Explaining, and Correcting Misleading Visualizations using Large Language Models
Writer-Defined AI Personas for On-Demand Feedback Generation

FC070.label: iterative revision loop

FC071.definition: The process pauses for a person to approve, confirm or take responsibility before continuing: accountability checkpoints, review gates, confirmation steps, deliberate friction before a consequential act.

examples.title: To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-assisted Decision-making
Towards Human-AI Synergy in UI Design: Leveraging LLMs for UI Generation with Intent Clarification and Alignment

FC071.label: human decision checkpoint or gate

FC072.definition: Assigns distinct parts of the work to different parties, human or machine: human-AI task splits, role separation, distributed expertise, staged division of diagnostic labour, complementary capability allocation.

examples.title: SET-PAiREd: Designing for Parental Involvement in Learning with an AI-Assisted Educational Robot
RECOVER: Designing a Large Language Model-based Remote Patient Monitoring System for Postoperative Gastrointestinal Cancer Care

FC072.label: division of labour across agents

FC073.definition: Passes accumulated work, context or findings from one party or stage to the next in usable form: handoff records, discovery handoffs, cross-stage integration, transferable analysis packages.

examples.title: ChunkyEdit: Text-first video interview editing via chunking
Beyond the Waiting Room: Patient’s Perspectives on the Conversational Nuances of Pre-Consultation Chatbots

FC073.label: handoff of work state

FC074.definition: Coordinates which action, tool, resource or participant is engaged when: action routing, orchestration of components, turn allocation, delegation of sensing, automation of a workflow step.

examples.title: Mentigo: An Intelligent Agent for Mentoring Students in the Creative Problem Solving Process
Estimating Contribution Quality in Online Deliberations Using a Large Language Model

FC074.label: orchestration and routing of actions

FC075.definition: Detects and mends a breakdown so the interaction can continue: conversational repair, recognition-error recovery, redirection after failure, re-entry after stalling, clarification of misunderstanding.

examples.title: UrbanClipAtlas: A Visual Analytics Framework for Event and Scene Retrieval in Urban Videos
From ‘Here’ to ‘There’: Exploring Proximity Semantics in Multimodal Data Exploration

FC075.label: interaction repair and recovery

FC076.definition: Work state is held so it can be left and returned to: resumable sessions, persistent state overviews, deferred-attention parking, analysis-state management across sessions.

examples.title: Clarifying Constraints in Interactive Robot Learning with Language Feedback
PromptCanvas: Composable Prompting Workspaces Using Dynamic Widgets for Exploration and Iteration in Creative Writing

FC076.label: resumable and persistent work state

FC077.definition: Puts something held in a person's head, or implicit in practice, into an inspectable external form: externalised concepts, preferences, strategies, expert knowledge, task state made visible outside the mind.

examples.title: Intent Tagging: Exploring Micro-Prompting Interactions for Supporting Granular Human-GenAI Co-Creation Workflows
Authoring LLM-Based Assistance for Real-World Contexts and Tasks

FC077.label: externalising internal structure into an artifact

FC078.definition: Marks meaning onto existing material in place: notes, tags, highlights, role labels, interpretive comments, marks on media or an artifact. Attaching to material, not building a separate structure.

examples.title: Grid Labeling: Crowdsourcing Task-Specific Importance from Visualizations
Getting on the Right Foot: Using Observational and Quantitative Methods to Evaluate Movement Disorders

FC078.label: annotation onto material

FC079.definition: Holds or returns something the person would otherwise forget: memory aids, recall cues, curated personal memory, retained context, reminders of prior activity, shared conversational memory.

examples.title: Explainable Recommendation for Repeat Consumption
Toward Enabling Natural Conversation with Older Adults via the Design of LLM-Powered Voice Agents that Support Interruptions and Backchannels

FC079.label: external memory and recall cue

FC080.definition: Records work, speech, observation or events in the moment for later use: live capture notation, in-situ recording, decision-intent capture, structured field capture, capture coordination.

examples.title: CommunityClick: Capturing and Reporting Community Feedback from Town Halls to Improve Inclusivity
MixTAPE: Mixed-initiative Team Action Plan Creation Through Semi-structured Notes, Automatic Task Generation, and Task Classification

FC080.label: capture of activity as it happens

FC081.definition: Revisits past states as a traversable record: playback of a process, generation-history navigation, session replay, branch histories, interaction-history views. Revisiting for sensemaking, not audit provenance.

examples.title: A Deixis-Centered Approach for Documenting Remote Synchronous Communication around Data Visualizations
RealityEffects: Augmenting 3D Volumetric Videos with Object-Centric Annotation and Dynamic Visual Effects

FC081.label: replay and history navigation

FC082.definition: A holding surface where material can be gathered, arranged and rearranged during the work: canvases, boards, curation workspaces, staging areas for ideas or evidence. The workspace itself is the facet.

examples.title: DATAWEAVER: Authoring Data-Driven Narratives through the Integrated Composition of Visualization and Text
RelianceScope: An Analytical Framework for Examining Students’ Reliance on Generative AI Chatbots in Problem Solving

FC082.label: reorganisable working workspace

FC083.definition: Renders meaning in sound, touch or force: sonification, auditory state encoding, haptic and tactile representation, vibration cues. The perceptual channel is the operation.

examples.title: RoboGraphics: Dynamic Tactile Graphics Powered by Mobile Robots
Leveraging Dynamic Audio-Tactile UIs to Assist Visually Impaired Users in Exploring Line Charts through Tactile Graphic Readers

FC083.label: non-visual sensory encoding

FC084.definition: Carries meaning from one perceptual channel into another, or composes several: cross-modal mapping, multimodal explanation composition, audio-to-visual and visual-to-tactile translation, modality restoration.

examples.title: Visualization of Speech Prosody and Emotion in Captions: Accessibility for Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing Users
OnomaCap: Making Non-speech Sound Captions Accessible and Enjoyable through Onomatopoeic Sound Representation

FC084.label: cross-modal translation

FC085.definition: Chooses how meaning maps onto visual form: colour, marks, glyphs, encoding choices, rendering cues, visual abstraction of a property. About the encoding decision, not the structure encoded.

examples.title: Net2Vis – A Visual Grammar for Automatically Generating Publication-Tailored CNN Architecture Visualizations
SEG-RobustEye: Understanding Medical Image Segmentation Models

FC085.label: visual encoding and graphical mapping

FC086.definition: Meaning is carried by the body or a physical object: gesture, movement, physical construction, enactment of an abstract process, proprioceptive and tangible representation, embodied demonstration.

examples.title: “Push-That-There”: Tabletop Multi-robot Object Manipulation via Multimodal ‘Object-level Instruction’
Modeling Adaptive Expression of Robot Learning Engagement and Exploring Its Effects on Human Teachers

FC086.label: embodied or physical enactment

FC087.definition: Recasts meaning in a figurative or symbolic register so it can be grasped differently: metaphors, analogies across domains, symbolic cues, anthropomorphic or narrative stand-ins for abstract state.

examples.title: Creative Sketching Partner: An Analysis of Human-AI Co-Creativity
Toward Affective Empathy via Personalized Analogy Generation: A Case Study on Microaggression

FC087.label: metaphorical or symbolic re-representation

FC088.definition: Adapts form so it can be perceived or understood by this person: accessibility authoring, readability and register adaptation, perceptual simplification, decluttering, plain restatement for a lay audience.

examples.title: MatplotAlt: A Python Library for Adding Alt Text to Matplotlib Figures in Computational Notebooks
Understanding Personalized Accessibility through Teachable AI: Designing and Evaluating Find My Things for People who are Blind or Low Vision

FC088.label: accessible or simplified presentation

FC089.definition: Puts non-verbal content into words: scene and image description, verbalised visual evidence, spoken account of a chart or space, described layout for non-visual access.

examples.title: VRSight: An AI-Driven Scene Description System to Improve Virtual Reality Accessibility for Blind People
From Screen Reading to “Scene Reading” in SceneVR: Touch-Based Interaction Techniques for Use in Virtual Reality by Blind and Low-Vision Users

FC089.label: verbal description of perceptual content

FC090.definition: A representation several people build and hold together: shared workspaces, jointly authored maps, collective artifacts, evolving shared case context. Shared authorship is the operation.

examples.title: Cultivating Spoken Language Technologies for Unwritten Languages
Documenting Data Production Processes: A Participatory Approach for Data Work

FC090.label: shared co-constructed representation

FC091.definition: Makes other people's activity, opinion, endorsement or participation legible: peer signals, endorsement counts, discussion intensity, participation disparity, aggregated human judgments, collective attention.

examples.title: Supporting Mixed-Presence Awareness across Wall-Sized Displays Using a Tracking Pipeline based on Depth Cameras
“It would work for me too”: How Online Communities Shape Software Developers’ Trust in AI-Powered Code Generation Tools

FC091.label: visibility of others' state and judgment

FC092.definition: Positions the person to see from another vantage: audience perspective on a draft, other-role viewpoints, reframed spatial or conceptual standpoints, interpretive lenses adopted deliberately.

examples.title: See Widely, Think Wisely: Toward Designing a Generative Multi-agent System to Burst Filter Bubbles
Proxona: Supporting Creators’ Sensemaking and Ideation with LLM-Powered Audience Personas

FC092.label: perspective-taking and viewpoint framing

FC093.definition: Organises how people put views to each other and reach a position: structured argument exchange, perspective confrontation, collective reflection, joint appraisal and alignment procedures.

examples.title: Wikibench: Community-Driven Data Curation for AI Evaluation on Wikipedia
Plurals: A System for Guiding LLMs Via Simulated Social Ensembles

FC093.label: structured deliberation and perspective exchange

FC094.definition: Assigns an identity or role to a participant or agent that shapes how the exchange proceeds: persona-mediated dialogue, scripted roles, declared interlocutor identity, multi-agent viewpoint casts.

examples.title: EyeSee: Enhancing Art Appreciation through Anthropomorphic Interpretations from Multiple Perspectives
Persona-L has Entered the Chat: Leveraging LLMs and Ability-based Framework for Personas of People with Complex Needs

FC094.label: role or persona framing of the interaction

FC095.definition: Governs what about a person or their data is revealed and to whom: consent controls, privacy-preserving generalisation, selective surfacing, sensing delegation, disclosure timing and trade-off settings.

examples.title: Exploring the Needs of Users for Supporting Privacy-Protective Behaviors in Smart Homes
Beyond Affirmative Consent: Creating Alternative Models for Consent to Computer-Mediated Sexual Activity Through Social VR for Online Dating

FC095.label: disclosure and privacy control

FC096.definition: A safe stand-in world or partner for practising something before doing it for real: rehearsal environments, practice scripts, simulated collaborators or clients, role-play for skill.

examples.title: Beyond the “Industry Standard”: Focusing Gender-Affirming Voice Training Technologies on Individualized Goal Exploration
Pattern analysis of ambitious science talk between preservice teachers and AI-powered student agents

FC096.label: simulated environment for rehearsal

FC097.definition: Builds hypothetical situations and plays them out: scenario specification, situation modelling, what-if worlds, held-out condition testing, speculative futures examined as objects.

examples.title: SimSpark: Interactive Simulation of Social Media Behaviors
Tangible Scenography as a Holistic Design Method for Human-Robot Interaction

FC097.label: scenario construction and what-if exploration

FC098.definition: The person perturbs a system or model and observes the response to learn how it works: interactive probes, black-box behaviour testing, component ablation, parameter-effect exploration, impact probing.

examples.title: Exposing the Ideology of Large Language Models with Creative Practices
The Prompt Artists

FC098.label: system-behaviour probing

FC099.definition: The amount or intensity of help changes with the person's state or over time: fading scaffolds, difficulty progression, contingent pacing of support, adaptive assistance levels, timing of when help arrives.

examples.title: Exploring the Design Space of Cognitive Engagement Techniques with AI-Generated Code for Enhanced Learning
Exploratory Assessment of Learning in an Intelligent Text Framework

FC099.label: graduated or faded support

FC100.definition: Information is released in stages, on request or as readiness allows: progressive disclosure, staged revelation, detail on demand, layered explanation depth. About release schedule, not level of abstraction.

examples.title: From Screen Reading to “Scene Reading” in SceneVR: Touch-Based Interaction Techniques for Use in Virtual Reality by Blind and Low-Vision Users
Your Model Is Unfair, Are You Even Aware? Inverse Relationship Between Comprehension and Trust in Explainability Visualizations of Biased ML Models

FC100.label: progressive disclosure of detail

FC101.definition: Explains what something in the domain means: definitions, concept clarification, terminology explanation, domain background, explanatory content about the subject rather than about the system.

examples.title: Skeptik: A Hybrid Framework for Combating Potential Misinformation in Journalism
Exploring Personalized Health Support through Data-Driven, Theory-Guided LLMs: A Case Study in Sleep Health

FC101.label: conceptual explanation of domain meaning

FC102.definition: Supplies a concrete instance done well, to study or imitate: worked examples, exemplars, model answers, demonstration cases, reference performances, illustrative applications.

examples.title: StratIncon Detector: Analyzing Strategy Inconsistencies Between Real-Time Strategy and Preferred Professional Strategy in MOBA Esports
SkinGEN: an Explainable Dermatology Diagnosis-to-Generation Framework with Interactive Vision-Language Models

FC102.label: worked example or exemplar

FC103.definition: Situates a newcomer in a task, interface or collaboration before real work: orientation overviews, onboarding tours, task framing at the outset, preparatory instruction, what-this-is explanations.

examples.title: Responding to Generative AI Technologies with Research-through-Design: The Ryelands AI Lab as an Exploratory Study
Improving Students Argumentation Learning with Adaptive Self-Evaluation Nudging

FC103.label: orientation and onboarding

FC104.definition: Organises a sequence of learning or practice over sessions: curricula, learning pathways, practice routing, prerequisite structure, personalised progression through content.

examples.title: TSConnect: An Enhanced MOOC Platform for Bridging Communication Gaps Between Instructors and Students in Light of the Curse of Knowledge
How Learner Control and Explainable Learning Analytics on Skill Mastery Shape Student Desires to Finish and Avoid Loss in Tutored Practice

FC104.label: curriculum and learning-path structuring

FC105.definition: The system assigns meaning categories, labels or interpretations to content: automatic tagging, generated labels for clusters or patterns, machine classification of behaviour, inferred themes.

examples.title: Explainable XR: Understanding User Behaviors of XR Environments using LLM-assisted Analytics Framework
A representation framework of product–service systems

FC105.label: machine-generated semantic labelling

FC106.definition: The person applies or builds meaning categories over material: qualitative coding, sorting into concepts, boundary construction, category refinement, human labelling workflows.

examples.title: Rideshare Transparency: Translating Gig Worker Insights on AI Platform Design to Policy
CollabCoder: A Lower-barrier, Rigorous Workflow for Inductive Collaborative Qualitative Analysis with Large Language Models

FC106.label: human semantic coding and categorisation

FC107.definition: Reduces content to its gist: summaries, syntheses of sources, thematic condensation, recaps, compression of repeated structure. Condensing content, not an overview of a whole collection's structure.

examples.title: InsightBridge: Enhancing Empathizing with Users through Real-Time Information Synthesis and Visual Communication
MedTutor: A Retrieval-Augmented LLM System for Case-Based Medical Education

FC107.label: summarisation and condensation

FC108.definition: Recasts content in a different representational kind while keeping its meaning: prose to structure, qualitative to quantitative, narrative to work items, schema-guided substitution, format conversion.

examples.title: StructVizor: Interactive Profiling of Semi-Structured Textual Data
Empowering Healthcare Practitioners with Language Models: Structuring Speech Transcripts in Two Real-World Clinical Applications

FC108.label: semantic transformation into another form

FC109.definition: Assembles what is known about one entity, concept or case into a single characterisation: entity profiles, case summaries, concept browsers, per-item dossiers drawn from many sources.

examples.title: Proxona: Supporting Creators’ Sensemaking and Ideation with LLM-Powered Audience Personas
PolicyCraft: Supporting Collaborative and Participatory Policy Design through Case-Grounded Deliberation

FC109.label: entity or concept profile

FC110.definition: Proposes the next piece of the person's own artifact in place: autocompletion, suggested continuations, inline rewrites, relational completion, drafting the next sentence or element.

examples.title: Effidit: An Assistant for Improving Writing Efficiency
Plume: Scaffolding Text Composition in Dashboards

FC110.label: completion and continuation of content

grouping_rationale: The overview relates the task meaning represented to the contribution a person can make through it. Representations can be authored by AI, people or both. Its eighteen illustrated relations explain the existing category definitions; they are not independent axes or new code assignments. The original five families remain metadata for coding, counts and compatible navigation. Within each category, named branches retain all 110 facets exactly once. No frequency threshold or top-k selection is used.

reading_relation_scope: Editorial explanations of existing definitions, not new coded tiers, category-to-axis assignments, measured activities or learning outcomes. Multiple relations can combine in one mechanism. Form, timing, agency and social arrangement can vary across relations; the marked categories expose mixed dimensions without changing their source memberships.

reading_relations.human_activity:
Trace a result;
check its grounds

State intentions;
set terms for work

Edit, steer, override
or reverse actions

Assess an attempt;
check and adjust

Study or imitate;
use changing help

Allocate, hand off
or resume work
reading_relations.representation:
Stages and roles;
gates and state

scope: Eighteen representation-participation relations explain 110 design distinctions. Five original coding families remain available for counts and navigation. Codes can overlap within a mechanism; the maps explain design possibilities, not observed activities or effects.
